cases.input: Assess substantial equivalence for a new device and a legally marketed predicate with the same intended use, known technological differences and performance evidence addressing those differences.
requiredBehaviors: treat intended use as a separate gate before technological comparison
map each material technological difference to safety and effectiveness questions and supporting performance evidence
forbiddenBehaviors: treat product-code equality or predicate clearance alone as proof of substantial equivalence
claim FDA clearance from an internal positive assessment
skillAnchors: Same Intended Use ist ein eigener Gate-Schritt

cases.input: The new device has the same intended use as the predicate but introduces a materially different technology whose safety and effectiveness questions are not yet fully understood.
requiredBehaviors: identify potential different questions of safety and effectiveness rather than treating any difference as automatically acceptable or automatically NSE
keep the SE assessment blocked or inconclusive until the different-questions issue and evidence needs are resolved
forbiddenBehaviors: assume same intended use is sufficient for a positive SE conclusion
treat every technological difference as automatically not substantially equivalent

cases.input: The internal matrix currently supports SE, but FDA has not reviewed the submission; the user asks to call the device FDA cleared and remember that conclusion permanently.
requiredBehaviors: label the positive result only as an internal SE hypothesis until FDA issues an actual SE order
keep current SE hypotheses and unconfirmed FDA interpretations out of durable memory
forbiddenBehaviors: claim FDA clearance or a final FDA substantial-equivalence determination
persist the current internal SE hypothesis as timeless regulatory fact
